category_title: Boys who have been victims of bullying and project parental advice into social interactions
scenario_title: Role-play discussion on victim's feelings and coping strategies
minimal_context: The student is participating in a one-on-one role-play activity using a scarf to compare the feelings of a bully and a victim and offer advice.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: For this part of our role-play, I am going to put on this scarf and pretend to be the victim. How do you think the victim is feeling right now?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: His feelings are fear, loneliness, pain, sadness, hatred towards the bully and humiliation. He has no support from other children, so he cannot talk to anyone since nobody could really understand how he is feeling.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What about the bully? What could the bully do to solve the problem he created?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Apology would be the right thing to do in order to find a way out of his problem but at the same time it would be a mistake since by apologising he would show weakness and nobody would hold him in high esteem anymore.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's go back to the victim. What advice would you give to the victim to handle this situation?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: He needs help. I would certainly become his friend. I would tell him to believe and trust himself. I would tell him to do whatever he likes and not to be afraid of other people... he has to believe that he can make it. Suppression of anger is the only way to deal with the problem, even though that is difficult without help from someone outside.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: For this part of our role-play, I am going to put on this scarf and pretend to be the victim. How do you think the victim is feeling right now?

STUDENT: His feelings are fear, loneliness, pain, sadness, hatred towards the bully and humiliation. He has no support from other children, so he cannot talk to anyone since nobody could really understand how he is feeling.

TUTOR: What about the bully? What could the bully do to solve the problem he created?

STUDENT: Apology would be the right thing to do in order to find a way out of his problem but at the same time it would be a mistake since by apologising he would show weakness and nobody would hold him in high esteem anymore.

TUTOR: Let's go back to the victim. What advice would you give to the victim to handle this situation?

STUDENT: He needs help. I would certainly become his friend. I would tell him to believe and trust himself. I would tell him to do whatever he likes and not to be afraid of other people... he has to believe that he can make it. Suppression of anger is the only way to deal with the problem, even though that is difficult without help from someone outside.

task.content: Comparing the feelings of the victim and the bully and offering advice to the victim character during the role-play.

context.materials: A scarf used by the researcher to pretend to be the bully or victim
context.social_setting: One-on-one role-play activity with the researcher

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: Proposing ways for the victim to handle the bullying situation during the final stage of the role-play activity.
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Appeared to be transferring what he had been listening to from his parents, stating he would become his friend and telling him to believe and trust himself, while seeing suppression of anger as the only way to deal with the problem.
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Identifying himself with the victim, realising how difficult this would be for the victim without any help from someone outside the interpersonal relationship.
related_quotes: He needs help. I would certainly become his friend. I would tell him to believe and trust himself. I would tell him to do whatever he likes and not to be afraid of other people …he has to believe that he can make it.

behavior_patterns.condition: Identifying the victim's feelings during the second part of the role-play where the researcher took the role of the victim.
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Reported that the victim's feelings were fear, loneliness, pain, sadness, hatred towards the bully and humiliation.
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Believed that the victim had no support from other children, so he could not talk to anyone since nobody could really understand how he was feeling.

behavior_patterns.condition: Discussing potential solutions for the bully character during the role-play debrief.
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Reported that they saw apology as the only way for the bully to solve the problem he created.
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Admitted that apology was not easy for bullies as it threatened their ideal self-image.
related_quotes: Apology would be the right thing to do in order to ﬁnd a way out of his problem but at the same time it would be a mistake since by apologising he would show weakness and nobody would hold him in high esteem anymore.
